children: , China's e-commerce and cloud-computing giant, confronted fresh U.S. allegations over large-scale AI-model distillation. Its American depositary shares dropped approximately 2.6% to $109.79 during Wednesday trading as investors weighed the threat of another technology clash between Washington and Beijing.

The federal advisory identified six Chinese AI developers and alleged that Alibaba tapped outputs from American models to accelerate development of its Qwen family. Model distillation is widely used across the AI industry, but U.S. agencies described the alleged scale and tactics as malicious. China rejected the claims as unsupported by the facts and the law, according to Reuters.

The timing is uncomfortable. Alibaba's AI Cloud and Compute Services produced 48.44 billion yuan in quarterly revenue, jumping 45% and representing roughly 18% of total sales. The image adds a valuation twist: the $109.79 share price sits 8.27% below the $119.69 GF Value estimate, suggesting the market is already discounting part of the regulatory risk. The advisory does not prove Alibaba's cloud revenue is under pressure, but tighter access controls, possible sanctions and higher compliance costs could complicate its push to make Qwen a global AI platform.

title: Alibaba Drops 2.6% as U.S. Turns AI Distillation Into a Security Threat
